request.description: At Fonontech, our vision is to pioneer a transformative and sustainable era in semiconductor packaging industry through our proprietary cutting-edge technology, Impulse Printing. Originating from extensive research and development at the Dutch leading Applied Research Institute TNO, the Impulse Printing technology has the unprecedented scalability, accuracy, and throughput for both 2D and 3D interconnect printing for the billion-dollar semiconductor and micro-LED packaging industry. The technology can attain feature sizes ranging from <10 µm to >100 µm in 3D, with the highest throughput and lowest cost of ownership, providing major competitive edge particularly in the critical lower feature range essential for enabling product miniaturization. Impulse Printing, distinguished by minimal cost of ownership and facility footprint, is safeguarded by 14 patents. It is slated for direct sales to high-volume electronic device manufacturers or through system integrators securing the company a revenue of €533 M by 2030.

projectAnswers.question: Is your Impulse Printing development still in progress, or have you already completed the core research and prototyping work?
projectAnswers.answer: Core development done; we are now building for commercial production
projectAnswers.quote: Applications for projects that have already been completed will be rejected; ongoing projects are assessed case-by-case with no reimbursement for costs incurred before submission.

projectAnswers.question: Who buys your Impulse Printing systems: the electronics manufacturers you describe, system integrators who resell them, or both?

projectAnswers.answer: Tooling and processes to scale from pilot to production volumes

derivable in principle from `private_funding_events` — a source no public award appears in, so it could not leak — but that table is not in `public/data/companies_index.json`, the one committed artifact this resolver may read. A build gate may not depend on gitignored data. 12 comparators; the honest fix is upstream in the index build.
nothing in the corpus states whether a company has a lender.

no ultimate-control data. Note the corpus is Europe-scoped, so answering `no` for everyone would look right and would be an assumption, not a fact.

the GBER and de minimis exclusions are self-declared and nothing in the register records them for a beneficiary. Pinning `none` would be an ANSWER — the permissive one — asserted on behalf of 7,095 companies we have not asked.
a stated willingness, not a fact. Nothing states it.
a stance about the future. Its job is the CURE on an establishment blocker, and the harness grades retrieval, not advice.
a founder's own timing. The award's grant date is when the money arrived, not when they needed it, and it is on the won award.
